_comment: ROM source archives on archive.org. 'loggedin'/restricted items need ia_creds.txt. layout: direct=/download/<item>/<prefix><name><suffix>; zip=that file is a per-game zip, extract the disc image. Match by fuzzy title+region, ALWAYS verify against the RA hash before install (cart=headerless/plain MD5; disc=app hasher via worker container).

homebrew_sources._comment: Approved for ALL systems (homebrew/aftermarket long tail). itch.io is NOT HTTP-scrapable (JS/bot shell; needs a headless browser or its API + a claimed game), and GB Studio titles are often browser-play-only there — so these feed the DROP-OFF workflow: the Missing page links to the source, you download, drop into <canonical>/dropoff, and process-dropoff hashes+files it. Homebrew Hub serves direct GB/GBC/GBA ROM downloads and is a candidate for real auto-sourcing later.

planetvb.note: Planet Virtual Boy homebrew. HTTP-scrapable: game page /homebrew/<slug>/ -> download page /downloads/<id>/ -> real file /downloads/<id>/get/<fileid> serves the raw headerless .vb (verified Virtual Picross v1.1 md5 bd7e84b0 == RA 2026-07-18)

disc._verify: app hasher in worker container (e.g. psx_chd=`rahash 12`, gamecube=16); rahash can't read .chd/.rvz directly except where the hasher extracts first

psx.note: Redump-exact USA 1G1R (Hearto, 2024). The other US source (PS1_US_CHD_Arquivista) is NOT Redump-exact — its dumps are named '<title> (US) - CD{n}.chd' and hash-mismatch every time, which is why Arc the Lad III, Final Fantasy IX, Dragon Warrior VII and both Wing Commanders sat unsourceable while their discs were sitting in this set. Zips hold bin/cue; the PSX hasher reads archives directly.
Redump JP CHDs under CHD-PSX-JAP/, exact Redump names incl (Disc n); title-fuzzy + hash-verified. Covers games absent from the Arquivista JP set (e.g. Book of Watermarks).

wii.note: alphabetized WiiWare/VC WADs by first letter — WiiWare/VC/Channels ONLY, no retail discs

PREFERRED retail Wii source, listed ahead of Arquivista on purpose. Six sibling items Part1..Part6, ~3740 per-game .zip across them, all regions, none dark, plain HTTP (no torrent/swarm). Filenames are EXACT Redump names, which is what makes them title-key-match RA hash names — the whole point, since Arquivista's '<Title> (US).rvz' labels are unreliable: 'Marble Saga - Kororinpa (US).rvz' there is 584MB and hashes f7342347…, i.e. the DEMO, while RA wants the 0.87GB (USA) (En,Fr,Es) dump. A game is in exactly ONE part, so all six must be registered. WiiHasher unzips it itself, so the plain _try path handles these.

Retail Wii discs, bare .rvz '<Title> (US).rvz'. US/EU are split A-Z as p1 (# - K) / p2 (L - S) / p3 (T - Z). DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Wii-p1-US-Arquivista and Wii-p2-EU-Arquivista are is_dark=true (withdrawn) — their /metadata still answers HTTP 200 with a ~260-byte dark stub and ZERO files, so a status-code check looks healthy while the source silently contributes nothing. Consequence: US titles # - K and EU titles L - S have no Arquivista route and fall through to the Minerva torrent. Re-check periodically; un-darking is the cheapest fix for that gap.

JP retail is a SINGLE part covering the whole alphabet (462 .rvz, 007 - Quantum of Solace -> Zenkoku Dekotora Matsuri), not split like US/EU. Does NOT contain Zero - Tsukihami no Kamen (it has Zero - Shinku no Chou); use wii-ntsc-j-redump below for that.

Wii NTSC-J Redump, 155 games as per-game .7z under 'Wii[NTSC-J]/<Title> [NTSC-J] [<GameID>]/'. _item_index keys on the BASENAME so the subdirs are transparent, and _title_key drops the [..] tags — 'Zero Tsukihami no Kamen [NTSC-J] [RVL-R4ZJ-JPN].7z' keys to ZERO TSUKIHAMI NO KAMEN and matches RA 34874. WiiHasher extracts .7z itself (_extract_disc_archive), so the plain HTTP _try path handles it — no torrent needed. Fills the JP gaps Wii-p1-JP-Arquivista lacks.

ndsi.note: FULL No-Intro Nintendo DSi (Digital) set, 1068 per-game .zip entries, hosted by minerva-archive.org (Myrient successor). Minerva is a TORRENT INDEX ONLY — its /rom?id=N pages expose no direct HTTP file URL, just the set .torrent + a magnet, which is why no download link is derivable by browsing. That is not a blocker: selective single-file leech via aria2c --select-file gets one ROM without the set. Verified 2026-08-05: 'Date Or Ditch (Europe, Australia).zip' -> afb08aa0bab13e132574db54af0f37d9, the exact RA-accepted dump. TRAP: the magnet's so= index is 0-BASED, aria2c --select-file is 1-BASED (so=292 is aria2c 293). The sourcer is immune because _torrent_index derives indexes from aria2c --show-files itself; only hand-reading so= off a magnet hits this.
